column4: Web analytics with Matomo service. A survey made in collaboration with Data Science Portuguese Association (sent to their associates: private entities - energy, communication, mobility, health, insurance, data, digital and technology enterprises - and public institutions - universities, R&D institutions, town halls). column7: We collect feedback through surveys and interviews from our initiatives such as webinars, conferences, and meetings with stakeholders from both the public and private sectors, as well as developers. column2:
Do you used the insights about portal usage and about the behaviour and needs of portal users to improve the portal accordingly?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please explain your process for improving the portal based on user insights and feedback
* If relevant, kindly highlight some improvements made in the past year
column7:
We collect several insights from the portal usage and needs that we strive to address. Typically, we include these improvements in our backlog after a thorough analysis of the effort and impact. These improvements must wait for their inclusion in the next project, or in urgent cases, the current project. An important step in this process is interacting with the uData framework development team to determine if some of these improvements are also in their roadmap.

From these insights, we can provide three concrete examples that were included in the previously mentioned backlog. The first was the need expressed by users to have a preview tool for structured data. This feature, developed by us, is already operational on dados.gov. The second was the need for a simple way for providers to check compliance with quality standards. This was implemented in due time by the uData team and is already functional on dados.gov. The last one addresses numerous complaints about the loss of thematic organization of the datasets in the new version of uData. To mitigate this problem, we are in discussions with the uData team to understand how we can provide users with a thematic approach to finding datasets. In summary, we collect feedback and take action to improve.

column2: 2.3 Data provision

To what degree do public sector data providers contribute data to the portal? 

For Explanation:
*Please describe what is the agreed approach.
* If less than the majority of data providers, please briefly explain why (e.g. technical incompatibilities, governance aspects, low awareness etc.).
column4:
Develop a governance structure, implement an Open data National Strategy, make data inventories/catalogs (that include information about data, data that cannot be opened, and data that can be opened and is not yet published), send a survey to the entities on data maturity (to each of the government agencies and the departments within), create awareness initiatives (webinar on open data concept and benefits, and the open data directive), and make a portal improvement. Also define methodologies to monitor/evaluate the impact of open data in areas such as government efficiency / public policies; reduction of operating costs; quality of public service provided; environmental impact; social impact; macroeconomic and microeconomic impact, etc. Design a user satisfaction survey.
Public sector data providers still demonstrate some reluctance, there is some cultural tightness, low awareness and data literacy, some departments have limited technological and human resources, and, most basilary, the lack of a general governance structure, in Portugal.
column7: As explained in question P2, the National Data Strategy has been finalized and is awaiting publication in the coming months. The effort to create data inventories/catalogues is progressing for most of the important entities that also represent many other entities. Both of these aspects will serve as leverage for the implementation of data governance in the Public Administration.

2.4 Portal sustainability

Does the national portal have a strategy to ensure its sustainability?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) provide the URL to this document and (2) describe the main measures to keep the portal running in the long-term and continue to serve its audience
column7:
In addition to all the initiatives implemented by the Portuguese Public Administration (PA) to maintain and evolve the portal, and with the intention of securing the portal’s relevance and importance, AMA has decided to assign a critical role to the portal. Leveraging the importance and impact that the “Portal Mais Transparência” (https://transparencia.gov.pt/pt/), a reuse of open data, has on transparency, citizen awareness, and participation, AMA decided that dados.gov will be the single point of access and aggregator for the high-quality data needed to update the “Portal Mais Transparência” in near real-time. This strategy, agreed upon by 9 entities (2 more to come), makes dados.gov a critical part of this reuse, which is internationally recognized and has a significant impact on the media and society (see attached document “Reuse_portal mais transparencia.pdf”). Without the option to participate in a marketplace where data monetization is a reality, we have concluded that the only strategy is to increase the positive impact and relevance of the portal to ensure its future financial sustainability.
Another contribution to the sustainability of the portal is the publication of open data from public service and feedback from citizens, which are the basis of an internal service of AMA, GIAP (see attach document "TICAPP202203_Guia de Utilização do Portal do gIAp_V2.0.pdf"), which contributes to the following objectives: Improve citizen satisfaction; Contribute to the continuous improvement of the quality of public service delivery, combining different channels: in person; voice and digital; Simplify administrative processes; and Evaluate the quality of services, taking into account the expectations of citizens.
Another relevant strategic decision is that it was decided to use an open source framework, uData, to improve sustainability.
